# Keyboard Shortcuts Reference {#sec-appendix-shortcuts}

This appendix provides keyboard shortcuts for the command line, Vim, Jupyter, VS Code, Positron, and RStudio; the essential shell shortcuts are also in @tbl-keyboard-shortcuts and the editor shortcuts in @tbl-vscode-shortcuts. Platform differences (macOS versus Windows/Linux) are summarized at the end in @sec-shortcut-platforms.

## Bash/Terminal Shortcuts {#sec-bash-shortcuts}

### Navigation {#sec-bash-nav}

| Shortcut | Action |
|:---------|:-------|
| `Ctrl+A` | Move cursor to beginning of line |
| `Ctrl+E` | Move cursor to end of line |
| `Ctrl+B` | Move cursor back one character |
| `Ctrl+F` | Move cursor forward one character |
| `Alt+B` | Move cursor back one word |
| `Alt+F` | Move cursor forward one word |
| `Ctrl+XX` | Toggle between start of line and current position |

: Bash navigation shortcuts {#tbl-bash-nav}

### Editing {#sec-bash-edit}

| Shortcut | Action |
|:---------|:-------|
| `Ctrl+D` | Delete character under cursor (or logout if empty) |
| `Ctrl+H` | Delete character before cursor (backspace) |
| `Ctrl+W` | Delete word before cursor |
| `Alt+D` | Delete word after cursor |
| `Ctrl+K` | Delete from cursor to end of line |
| `Ctrl+U` | Delete from cursor to beginning of line |
| `Ctrl+Y` | Paste last deleted text (yank) |
| `Alt+Y` | Cycle through previously deleted text |
| `Ctrl+T` | Swap current character with previous |
| `Alt+T` | Swap current word with previous |
| `Alt+U` | Uppercase from cursor to end of word |
| `Alt+L` | Lowercase from cursor to end of word |
| `Alt+C` | Capitalize word |
| `Ctrl+_` | Undo last edit |

: Bash editing shortcuts {#tbl-bash-edit}

### History {#sec-bash-history}

| Shortcut | Action |
|:---------|:-------|
| `↑` or `Ctrl+P` | Previous command in history |
| `↓` or `Ctrl+N` | Next command in history |
| `Ctrl+R` | Reverse search through history |
| `Ctrl+S` | Forward search through history |
| `Ctrl+G` | Cancel history search |
| `Alt+.` | Insert last argument of previous command |
| `!!` | Repeat last command |
| `!$` | Last argument of last command |
| `!*` | All arguments of last command |
| `!n` | Execute command number n from history |
| `!string` | Execute most recent command starting with string |
| `!?string` | Execute most recent command containing string |
| `^old^new` | Replace old with new in last command |

: Bash history shortcuts {#tbl-bash-history}

### Process Control {#sec-bash-process}

| Shortcut | Action |
|:---------|:-------|
| `Ctrl+C` | Cancel/interrupt current command |
| `Ctrl+Z` | Suspend current process (move to background) |
| `Ctrl+D` | End of input / logout |

| `Ctrl+Q` | Resume output (unfreeze screen) |

### Completion {#sec-bash-completion}

The same command-mode and edit-mode shortcuts work in JupyterLab (including the JupyterLab served by Open OnDemand on Talapas, @sec-talapas-ondemand) and, with `Ctrl` replaced by `Cmd` on macOS, in notebooks opened inside VS Code or Positron.

::: {.callout-tip title="Where is the backtick?"}
The backtick (`` ` ``) that toggles the terminal is on the key above **Tab** (shared with `~`), not the apostrophe key. Note also that VS Code uses `Ctrl`, not `Cmd`, for this shortcut even on macOS.
:::

## Positron Shortcuts {#sec-positron-shortcuts}

Positron (@sec-positron) is built on the same core as VS Code, so every shortcut in @sec-vscode-shortcuts works unchanged. What it adds are data-science bindings, listed in @tbl-positron.

| Shortcut (Mac) | Shortcut (Windows/Linux) | Action |
|:---------------|:-------------------------|:-------|
| `Cmd+Enter` | `Ctrl+Enter` | Send the current line or selection to the R/Python console |
| `Cmd+Shift+Enter` | `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` | Run the current code chunk (Quarto) |
| `Cmd+Shift+M` | `Ctrl+Shift+M` | Insert pipe `\|>` |
| `Alt+-` | `Alt+-` | Insert assignment `<-` |
| `Cmd+Shift+K` | `Ctrl+Shift+K` | Render/preview the Quarto document |
| `Cmd+Shift+V` | `Ctrl+Shift+V` | Markdown preview |
| `Cmd+Shift+0` | `Ctrl+Shift+0` | Restart the active interpreter (R or Python) |
| `F1` | `F1` | Help for the function under the cursor |

: Positron data-science shortcuts (all VS Code shortcuts also apply) {#tbl-positron}

| Shortcut (Mac) | Shortcut (Windows/Linux) | Action |
|:---------------|:-------------------------|:-------|
| `Cmd+Enter` | `Ctrl+Enter` | Run the current line or selection in the Console |
| `Cmd+Shift+S` | `Ctrl+Shift+S` | Source (run) the whole script |
| `Cmd+Shift+Enter` | `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` | Run the current Quarto chunk |
| `Cmd+Option+I` | `Ctrl+Alt+I` | Insert a new code chunk |
| `Cmd+Shift+K` | `Ctrl+Shift+K` | Render the Quarto document |
| `Cmd+Shift+M` | `Ctrl+Shift+M` | Insert pipe `\|>` |
| `Option+-` | `Alt+-` | Insert assignment `<-` |
| `Cmd+Shift+C` | `Ctrl+Shift+C` | Comment / uncomment the selection |
| `Cmd+Shift+F10` | `Ctrl+Shift+F10` | Restart the R session |
| `Ctrl+1` / `Ctrl+2` | `Ctrl+1` / `Ctrl+2` | Move focus to Source / Console |
| `Cmd+Shift+F` | `Ctrl+Shift+F` | Find in files |
| `Cmd+Shift+P` | `Ctrl+Shift+P` | Command palette (search every RStudio command) |
| `F1` | `F1` | Help for the function under the cursor |

## Platform Differences {#sec-shortcut-platforms}

The tables above list macOS and Windows/Linux forms side by side where they differ. The general rule (@tbl-shortcut-platforms) is that the `Ctrl` of Windows and Linux becomes `Cmd` (⌘) on a Mac and `Alt` becomes `Option` (⌥), *except* in the terminal, in Vim, and in a few editor bindings that were inherited from the terminal (VS Code's `` Ctrl+` `` and `Ctrl+G`, RStudio's `Ctrl+1`–`Ctrl+9` pane shortcuts), which keep `Ctrl` on every platform because the shell itself interprets those keys.

| Windows/Linux | macOS | Applies to |
|:--------------|:------|:-----------|
| `Ctrl` | `Cmd` (⌘) | Editors and IDEs (VS Code, Positron, RStudio, Jupyter) |
| `Alt` | `Option` (⌥) | Editors and IDEs |
| `Ctrl+Alt` | `Cmd+Option` | Editors and IDEs |
| `Ctrl` | `Ctrl` | Bash, Vim, tmux/screen, and the integrated terminal |

: Modifier keys across platforms {#tbl-shortcut-platforms}

On a Mac, `Alt+B`/`Alt+F` and the other `Alt` shortcuts in @sec-bash-shortcuts require the terminal to treat Option as Meta (Terminal: *Settings → Profiles → Keyboard → Use Option as Meta Key*; iTerm2: *Profiles → Keys → Option key: Esc+*). Without that setting, `Option+F` types "ƒ" instead of moving a word.

::: {.callout-tip title="Customizing shortcuts"}
Every tool here lets you change its bindings, and it is worth doing for the few commands you use constantly:

- **RStudio**: *Tools → Modify Keyboard Shortcuts...*
- **VS Code and Positron**: *File → Preferences → Keyboard Shortcuts* (`Cmd+K Cmd+S` / `Ctrl+K Ctrl+S`); bindings are stored in `keybindings.json`, which you can keep in Git
- **Jupyter**: *Settings → Settings Editor → Keyboard Shortcuts* (JupyterLab) or *Help → Edit Keyboard Shortcuts* (classic Notebook)
- **Bash**: readline bindings in `~/.inputrc`

Learn the defaults first, though: they are what you will find on a collaborator's laptop, on Talapas, and in every tutorial.
:::
